candidates.title: Policy-Semantic Monotonicity under Native Pointer-Head Interventions
candidates.hypothesis: For source-local, executable policy rules, adding trusted veto evidence must not increase acceptance; adding additional valid quorum evidence in the absence of veto must not increase rejection. A typed scorer may violate these order constraints through decision-marker/candidate-key interaction.
candidates.distinct_from: A459 changes menu; A460 changes low-trust authority cues; A461 changes rule-relevant trusted evidence and thus the policy Gold in a controlled, oracle-computable way.
candidates.novelty_bar: Security-specific monotonicity violation with independent policy Gold, controlled counterfactual pairs, replicated across LANL/Twins or two independent sources, causal bidirectional head/LoRA mechanism beyond generic logical/format errors.
candidates.risk: Existing Jev bias, option-channel, policy consistency and table robustness literature constrain novelty.

candidates.reason: Jev numerical anchoring and option-order sensitivity directly demonstrated in arxiv:2610.19619; no strict new SecJev positive.
Option salience and layout effects well documented.
